templates.title: Discovery / feature / design
templates.useWhen: Explore a problem or decision, including a product with no PRD yet

templates.useWhen: Deliver accepted bounded scope with validation and closeout

templates.title: Work record and conditional design
templates.useWhen: Preserve independently owned plan, decisions, evidence and handoff

templates.title: Work registry format
templates.useWhen: Register work identities and exact source bindings; this is a schema, not a prose form

templates.title: New-project engineering playbook
templates.useWhen: Bootstrap and tailor engineering rules for a new project

templates.title: Adversarial invariant matrix
templates.useWhen: Plan positive/negative evidence for a governed slice

templates.title: Intent discovery
templates.useWhen: Define user, problem, outcome and unknowns before implementation

templates.title: Specification
templates.useWhen: Turn an accepted outcome into scoped, testable requirements

templates.title: Architecture review
templates.useWhen: Review significant technical choices and alternatives

templates.title: Invariant-to-test matrix and pre-implementation evidence
templates.useWhen: Map each requirement and failure to verifiable evidence

templates.title: Closeout
templates.useWhen: Use the existing completion and closeout requirements

templates.title: Source facts
templates.useWhen: Establish technical and external facts before choosing an implementation

templates.title: Human verification checklist
templates.useWhen: Make reviewer checks self-contained with sources and pass/fail criteria

templates.useWhen: Consult repository-specific examples; use the engineering playbook for the reusable scaffold

routes.question: What is NarraTwin and what works?
How do I investigate a user need or design?
How do I propose and scope a change?
What changed and how do I verify it?
What is done, pending and next?
Where are current limits and operational procedures?

impacts.updateWhen: User journey, requirements, interaction or accessibility changes
Interfaces, schema, tenant boundaries or migrations change
Grounding, model/prompt/evaluation or refusal behavior changes
Threats, privacy, dependencies, identity or secrets boundaries change
Deployment, reliability, restore, monitoring or cost behavior changes
Build, dependency, scanning or release controls change
Engineering workflow, source custody or validation rules change

guardrails: Work will use issue + branch + PR, not direct main commits.
No secrets or real provider keys will be committed.
Tests must run with mock/local providers and no paid provider requirement.
